newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland Orangemen call off flashpoint parades.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Orangemen call off flashpoint parades.

text.p: The Protestant Orange Order called off flashpoint parades in Northern Ireland this weekend to avoid possible loss of life after a tide of Catholic anger and a week of violence across the province.

The Order said in a statement late on Thursday night the violence had been inspired by Sinn Fein, political wing of IRA guerrillas fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, but added that it was calling off the parades "for the greater good of the province".
The decision, unprecedented in the organisation's centuries-old history, was greeted with relief by leaders on both sides of the province's religious and political divide.
The British and Irish governments, co-sponsors of Northern Ireland's battered peace process, gave it a warm welcome.
It ended a standoff between the Order and Catholic residents associations who had threatened mass demonstrations to block the parades which they regard as sectarian intimidation.

The Order, founded to celebrate its Protestant faith and British loyalty, called off parades in Belfast's Lower Ormeau Road and the towns of Newry and Armagh. It said it was rerouting a march in Londonderry.

"This week in particular has witnessed Sinn Fein/IRA inspired violence throughout the province and there are indications of more serious republican violence and actions deliberately designed to provoke members of the Orange Institution," the Armagh Order said in a statement.
The parades are held on the "Glorious 12th" of July, which marks a 1690 victory by a Protestant king over an invading Catholic monarch. It is the organisation's most cherished day.
Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam said the decision would "be received with a great deal of relief and appreciation in Northern Ireland and beyond".
A spokesman for Irish Prime Minister Bertie Ahern said: "It is a very positive gesture by the Orange Order. The government believes it deserves an equally positive response from nationalists."
Jeffrey Donaldson, an Orange leader, said: "These decisions were decisions of local lodges. This is not something that was imposed on them. I must say they have my utmost admiration."
Police had voiced serious concern about the Lower Ormeau Road march, scene of violent confrontation in recent years.
The decision not to parade in the Belfast suburb was announced by the Ballynafeigh Orange Lodge at the Protestant end of the Lower Ormeau Road.
Outside the lodge a small but angry crowd gathered, plainly displeased at the decision. They jostled journalists, shouting obscenities and forcing them away from the lodge entrance.

The Order, which wants to maintain the province's 300-year-old union with Britain, had come under intense pressure to cancel the parades after week-long violence caused by a march through a Catholic area in the town of Portadown last Sunday.
A radical IRA splinter group, the Irish National Liberation Army, had threatened to attack Orange Order members if they paraded along the Lower Ormeau Road.

Political sources said Northern Ireland police chief Ronnie Flanagan told Orange leaders earlier in the day that he could not guarantee the safety of marchers in Belfast because of calls by Catholic residents assocations for mass protest.
Sir John Alderdice of the moderate Alliance Party said: "Good sense has won. The only losers are people who wanted trouble, who wanted violence."
Sinn Fein President Gerry Adams quickly issued a statement welcoming a decision he had campaigned for for years.
"I welcome these decisions and acknowledge their significance," he said. "I wish it had been made earlier."
He was referring to last Sunday's Orange Order parade through the Catholic Garvaghy Road area of Portadown which sparked the worst violence the province has seen for years.
Gerard Rice, a nationalist leader from the Lower Ormeau Road, welcomed the Orange Order's decision but said: "I think it's sad that I have to be grateful to be able to live free from fear."
